newsitem.title: UK: Elf adds Gallic sophistication to UK petrol stations.
newsitem.headline: Elf adds Gallic sophistication to UK petrol stations.

text.p: French oil company Elf brought a dash of Gallic sophistication to the forecourts of British petrol stations on Friday when it opened its first luxury store on a forecourt in south London.

Customers at the Elf station in the leafy south London suburb of Balham will now be able to stock up on everything and anything from mussels in white wine to freshly baked bread when they pull in to top up their tanks.

The store's opening marks the launch of Elf UK's -- a subsidiary of Elf Aquitaine -- planned "Le Shop" chain being run in alliance with supermarket chain Somerfield. The alliance hopes to open another 30 stores by the end of the year.
"The shop is big enough to do your weekly shop with a wide variety and range of products." said Elf spokesman Alex Blake-Milton.
"This is an exciting initiative," he said. "Where else could you get mussels in white wine or smoked salmon at your forecourt?"
